TRAMO-SEATS seasonal adjustment (JDemetra+ v3)

Source: R/models.R
TRAMOSEATS.Rd

Defines a TRAMO-SEATS model to be used inside fabletools::model(). The model is estimated with rjd3tramoseats::jtramoseats() and the Java result is kept in the fitted model. Arguments and specials are the same as for X13().

Usage

TRAMOSEATS(
  formula,
  spec = c("rsafull", "rsa0", "rsa1", "rsa2", "rsa3", "rsa4", "rsa5"),
  context = NULL,
  ref_spec = spec,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula: the name of the variable to adjust (y), or y ~ specials (see jd3_specials).

spec

Base specification: a character name or a specification object from rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats_spec().

context

A modelling context created with rjd3toolkit::modelling_context() (e.g. for custom calendars), or NULL.

ref_spec

Reference specification stored in the model: it is the reference of the refresh policies used by refit() and stream(). Defaults to spec, that is the specification before its modification by the specials.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A model definition that can be passed to fabletools::model(). Once fitted, the mable column contains a jd3_model object. Use components() to get the decomposition as a dable (columns trend, seasonal, irregular and season_adjust).

See also

X13(), TRAMO(), jd3_specials, jd3_model_methods

Examples

y <- tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers)

mb <- model(y, ts = TRAMOSEATS(value))
components(mb)
#> # A dable: 144 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 ts     1949 Jan   112  123.    0.913     0.998          123.
#>  2 ts     1949 Feb   118  124.    0.947     1.00           125.
#>  3 ts     1949 Mar   132  126.    1.05      0.996          125.
#>  4 ts     1949 Apr   129  127.    1.01      1.00           127.
#>  5 ts     1949 May   121  127.    0.950     1.00           127.
#>  6 ts     1949 Jun   135  126.    1.07      1.000          126.
#>  7 ts     1949 Jul   148  126.    1.18      0.995          125.
#>  8 ts     1949 Aug   148  127.    1.17      0.999          127.
#>  9 ts     1949 Sep   136  128.    1.06      1.00           129.
#> 10 ts     1949 Oct   119  130.    0.922     0.996          129.
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

# Fit both methods side by side and plot the seasonally adjusted series
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value), ts = TRAMOSEATS(value))
if (requireNamespace("ggtime", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::autoplot(components(mb))
}
